entries.competence: Demonstrating effects and application of waves
entries.objective: Understand and the laws and principles of waves
entries.teaching_act: Guide students to brainstorm the concept of waves while they are in groups. Lead students to demonstrate the production of waves using rope, ripple tank and tuning fork.
entries.learning_act: to sit in group and discuss the concept of waves.
entries.materials: Rope, ripple tank, tuning fork.
entries.assessment: Through quiz ask students to explain the concept of waves, wavelength, frequency and velocity of wave. Ask students to explain mechanical waves and electromagnetic waves.

entries.competence: Demonstrating effects and application of waves
entries.objective: Understand and the laws and principles of waves
entries.teaching_act: Using questions and answers technique to assist students to explain the terms wavelength (), frequency (f) and velocity (v) of the wave. Guide students to identify the types of waves.
entries.learning_act: to explain the terms wave length, frequency, and velocity of the wave . to take notes. students in groups to identify mechanical waves and electromagnetic waves.
entries.materials: Charts showing graph of displacement against time. C.R.O. Helical spring Drum Light
entries.assessment: Through quiz ask students to explain the concept of waves, wavelength, frequency and velocity of wave. Ask students to explain mechanical waves and electromagnetic waves.

entries.period: using demonstration in class, guide students to explain the behavior of waves, reflection, diffraction and interference. guide students to brainstorm on the applications of reflection, refraction, diffraction and interference of waves. guide students to present the applications of behavior of waves. assist students to sit in groups to demonstrate behavior of waves.
entries.teaching_act: to explain reflection, refraction and interference. using think- pair – shave technique, students to mention the application of reflection, refraction, diffraction and interference of waves. while in group students to demonstrate reflection, refraction, diffraction and interference of waves
entries.learning_act: Ripple tank, rectangular prism, and vibrator. Radio TV Mobile phone. Ripple tank Rectangular prisms. Vibrator.
entries.references: Group students and give quiz to explain the behavior of waves. Move around the groups and assess students performance on demonstrating the behavior of waves

entries.teaching_act: using question and answer technique to assist students to describe the propagation of mechanical waves. guide students to demonstrate the propagation of mechanical waves.
entries.learning_act: to sit in group to describe the propagation of mechanical waves.
entries.materials: Slinky spring. Tuning fork. Ripple tank. Rope.
entries.assessment: ask students to note down the criteria of propagation of mechanical waves.

entries.teaching_act: through questions and answer technique explain the propagation of electromagnetic waves. guide students to demonstrate the propagation of e.m. waves. Guide students to determine the relationship between frequency, speed and wavelength. Group students in two and guide them to determine the refractive index of glass. Guide students to use the formula to find refractive index of different materials.
entries.learning_act: to discuss the propagation of e.m. waves. to describe frequency from equation to state S. I. unit of frequency. to determine the refractive index of a glass black and submit their results to the teacher.
entries.materials: Chart showing the e.m. spectrum. Chart showing the relationship between frequency, speed and wavelength. Glass block. Optical pins. White sheet. Protector. Ruler. Drawing board.
entries.references: Slinky spring. Tuning fork. Ripple tank. Rope.
entries.remarks: ask students to explain propagation of e.m.w. ask students to state the S.I. unit of frequency. assess students while they are doing practical.

entries.period: Guide students to identify sources of sound waves. Using questions and answer technique guide students to explain the concept of audibility range.
entries.teaching_act: Students to produce sound waves by using different sources of sound. Students to explain the concept of audibility range.
entries.learning_act: Drum Guitar Whistle Turning Model of ear. Table with audibility range.
entries.references: Ask students to explain different sources of sound waves. Ask students to explain the concept of audibility range.

entries.period: Guide students to describe the perception of hearing. Guide students to demonstrate the production of an echo and explain the concept of reverberation of sound.
entries.teaching_act: Students to describe the perception of hearing. To explain the concept of echo and reverberation of sound.
entries.learning_act: Model of the human ear. Tall wall Hall/studio. Sound absorbing materials (cloth, spongy material)
entries.references: Ask students to explain the concept of echo and reverberation of sound.
entries.assessment: Ask students to explain different sources of sound waves. Ask students to explain the concept of audibility range.

entries.week: Speed of sound in air. Musical sound
entries.sub_topic: Using drum and stop watch, guide students to measure the speed of sound in air. Using different musical instruments, guide students to explain the concept of musical sound. Lead students to identify factors affecting loudness, pitch and quality of musical sound.
entries.period: Students to perform an experiment to measure the velocity of sound in air. Students to give the meaning of music and noise. Students to identify factors affecting loudness, pitch and quality of musical sound.
entries.teaching_act: Stop watch Drum Tape measure Guitar Drum Sonometer Turning forks Violin Flute Microphone C.R.O.
entries.materials: Assess students’ participation on measuring velocity of sound in air. Give the class work asking students to explain factors affecting loudness, pitch and quality of musical sound.
entries.references: Ask students to explain the concept of echo and reverberation of sound.
entries.assessment: Ask students to explain different sources of sound waves. Ask students to explain the concept of audibility range.

entries.teaching_act: Organize the study strip to visit a musical band or studio to identify different types of musical instruments. Lead students to explain the terms of standing (stationery) waves
entries.learning_act: By listening students to distinguish different musical instruments by the sound they produce. Students to explain the terms nodes, antinodes, crest and trough as applied in stationery waves.
entries.materials: Pipes, string, membrane, and electronic instruments. Helical spring. Vibrator Marker pen White sheet Motor and battery Rubber band
entries.assessment: Ask students if they can identify the different musical instrument. Give quiz on terms used in stationery waves

entries.teaching_act: Guide students to perform an experiment to determine the factors which affect the frequency of a note by stretched string.
entries.learning_act: Students to carry out an experiment to determine factors which affect the frequency of a note produced by a stretched string. Students to determine the frequency of a musical note.
entries.materials: String Sonometer Guitar Turning fork
entries.assessment: Assess students’ performance and participation on finding the frequency of a stretched string.

entries.period: Lead students to distinguish between fundamental note and overtones. Lead students to explain the concept of resonances as applied to sound. With the guidance of an expert, support student to construct a simple musical instrument. Guide students to explain the concept of the electromagnetic spectrum. Guide students to draw and label the electromagnetic spectrum. Guide students to detect infrared radiation, visible and u-v rays
entries.teaching_act: Students to distinguish between fundamental note and overtones. Students to explain the concept of resonance as applied to sound. Students to initiate the construction of simple musical instruments. Students to explain the concept of electromagnetic spectrum. Students to identify bands of the lectromagnetic spectrum. Students in groups to detect infrared rays, visible and U-V rays.
entries.learning_act: Resonance tube/burette. Turning fork. String Nails Membrane Metal can Piece of wood. Glass prism Chart of rain bow. Thermometer Iron Heater Sun rays.
entries.references: Through questions and answers assess students on distinguish between fundamental note and overtones Assess students work i.e. their musical instruments they made. Ask students to identify the bands of electromagnetic spectrum. Asses and record the participation of students on detecting those rays

entries.sub_topic: Application of e.m.w in daily life
entries.teaching_act: Guide students to identify the application of microwaves, radio waves, and infrared, -rays and x-rays. Explain the importance of electromagnetic waves in Agriculture and climate.
entries.learning_act: Through think-pair-share technique Students to identify the applications of microwaves, radio-waves, infrared, -rays and x-rays. Students to carryout project work on the importance of electromagnetic waves in agriculture and climate.
entries.references: Give test to check if students can identify the application of e.m.w in daily life.

entries.assessment: Give a home asking students to write short notes on how electric current produce magnetic field and identify patterns of the field lines.

Guide students to determine the attraction and repulsion of current flowing through parallel wire.
entries.teaching_act: To state the right hand rule and cork screw rule. Students to identify the direction of the magnetic field due to current carrying conductor. students to determine the direction of the force acting on a current carrying conductor. students to state Fleming’s left hand rule. to perform experiment to show the directions of repulsive and attractive force.

entries.references: Ask students to state right hand rule and cork screw rule. Assess students involvement on determining the direction of magnetic field produced. Ask students to state Fleming’s left hand rule. Assess students’ performance on doing experiment.

entries.learning_act: Students, in group, to demonstrate the production of induced current using coil and magnet. Students to explain the concept of electromagnetic induction. entries.teaching_act: Guide students to explain the concept of self induction and mutual induction Using diagram describe the structure of the induction coil and how it works Explain to the students the flow of a.c and d.c from a coil rotating in a magnetic field. The teacher to explain the mode of action of a.c and d.c generators and how to convert a.c generator to d.c.
entries.learning_act: Students to explain the concept of self and mutual induction. Students to describe the mode of action of an induction coil. To explain the flow of a.c and d.c from a coil rotating in a magnetic field. Students to discuss the applications of a.c generator and the advantages of a.c generator over d.c generator.

entries.assessment: Ask students to construct simple step-up and step down transformer.
entries.remarks: Give a group work and ask students to write short notes on mode of action of induction coil. In group work ask students to write the notes on the mode of action of a.c and d.c generator

headers: Recognizing the importance and hazards of radioactive emissions.

entries.competence: Recognizing the importance and hazards of radioactive emissions.
entries.objective: Realize the importance and hazards of radioactive emission.
entries.teaching_act: Guide students to discuss the structure of the atoms while they sit in groups. Assist students to give the meaning of atomic number, mass number and isotopes of elements. Assist students to mention the existence of forces holding the nucleons.
entries.learning_act: to sit in group and discuss the structure of the atom. Using think-pair-share technique. Students to discuss the meaning of atomic number, mass number and isotopes of elements. Students in groups to mention the forces holding the nucleus.
entries.materials: Chart of atom Model of atom. Model showing atomic no., mass no. of elements. Charts showing electron and proton in an atom.
entries.assessment: Ask each group to describe the structure of the nucleus of an atom. Give class work testing students on atomic no., mass no., and isotopes of element and forces holding nucleus.

entries.period: The teacher to explain the concept of radioactivity. The teacher to highlight the properties of alpha () and Beta () and gamma () radiations.
entries.teaching_act: Students to explain the concept of radioactivity. While in groups, students to describe the properties of radiations emitted by radioactive substances.
entries.learning_act: Periodic table.
entries.references: Ask students to write few sentences to explain the concept of radioactivity. Give a quiz on properties of radiations emitted by radioactive substances.

entries.period: The teacher to highlight the nuclear changes due to the emission of , and radiations. Guide students on the detection of and rays using G-M counters, spark chamber or Wilson Cloud Chamber. Guide students to detect -rays using photographic plate.

entries.learning_act: Periodic emission. Chart showing emission of , and radiations. Chart showing the detectors.
entries.references: Ask students to explain the nuclear changes due to emission of, and radiations. Give students home work to write short notes on one of the detectors discussed.

entries.materials: Periodic table Chart of bomb adding elements.
entries.assessment: Ask students to distinguish between natural and artificial radioactivity. Arrange students in group to write method of producing and applications of artificial radioactivity.

entries.teaching_act: Teacher to explain the effects of nuclear radiations on human body. The teacher to highlight about protection from the nuclear radiations.
entries.learning_act: Students in group to explain the effect of nuclear radiation on human body. Students to demonstrate using role play on how to protect themselves from nuclear radiations.
entries.materials: Chart showing the hazards of radiations Pictures showing people working with radioactive materials.
entries.assessment: Ask students to explain effects of nuclear reactions of human body.

entries.objective: -do- Realize the importance and hazard of x-ray

entries.materials: Chart of nuclear power station.
entries.assessment: Give a quiz on nuclear fission and fusion. Each group to give their report and teacher to assess their presentation.

entries.objective: -do- Realize the importance and hazard of x-ray

entries.materials: Cathode ray tube. Chart showing cathode ray tube. TV Computer monitor. Charts of maltose cross and paddle wheel.
entries.assessment: Assess students on explaining the production of cathode rays. Ask students to state the properties of cathode rays.

entries.objective: Realize the importance and hazard of X-ray

Students to write notes on their educational trip.

entries.assessment: Group students and ask them to note down the structure and mode of action of X-rays tube. Give a quiz on soft and hard X-rays. Let students write the applications of X-rays.
